import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_files = {
    "source0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_0.csv",
    "source1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_1.csv",
    "source2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_2.csv",
    "source3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_3.csv",
    "source4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_4.csv",
    "source5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_5.csv",
    "source6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_6.csv",
    "source7": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_7.csv",
    "source8": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_8.csv",
    "source9": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_9.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source0"], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source1"], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source2"], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source3"], index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source4"], index_col=0)
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source5"], index_col=0)
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source6"], index_col=0)
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source7"], index_col=0)
df8 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source8"], index_col=0)
df9 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source9"], index_col=0)

# Step 2: Union all source tables that share the same schema and match target columns:
# Source tables with schema ['CANCELED', 'ROW_WID', 'ACCNT_LOC', 'ARPU', 'SES', 'HOME_PASSED', 'CUST_SINCE_DT', 'MONTHS_AGE', 'CANCEL_DT', 'CITY', 'POP']:
# These are df0, df2, df6, df7
# We union them vertically (concat)
df_union = pd.concat([df0, df2, df6, df7], ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: Join the unioned large dimension table (df_union) with all other aspect tables on ROW_WID
# Aspect tables:
# df1: ['ROW_WID', 'KEYWORDS_NUM']
# df3: ['ROW_WID', 'VISITS_NUM']
# df4: ['ROW_WID', 'COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM']
# df5: ['ROW_WID', 'TECHSUPPORT_NUM']
# df8: ['ROW_WID', 'INBOUND_CALLS_NUM']
# df9: ['ROW_WID', 'INTERACTIONS_NUM']

# We perform left joins on df_union (dimension table) with each aspect table on 'ROW_WID'

df_merged = df_union.merge(df1, on="ROW_WID", how="left")
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df3, on="ROW_WID", how="left")
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df4, on="ROW_WID", how="left")
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df5, on="ROW_WID", how="left")
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df8, on="ROW_WID", how="left")
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df9, on="ROW_WID", how="left")

# Step 4: Fill missing numeric columns (aspect tables) with 0 because counts/numbers likely default to 0 if missing
num_cols_fill_zero = [
    "KEYWORDS_NUM",
    "VISITS_NUM",
    "COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM",
    "TECHSUPPORT_NUM",
    "INBOUND_CALLS_NUM",
    "INTERACTIONS_NUM",
]
df_merged[num_cols_fill_zero] = df_merged[num_cols_fill_zero].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Step 5: Ensure data types match target schema exactly
# Target schema:
# ['CANCELED': int, 'ROW_WID': int, 'ACCNT_LOC': int, 'ARPU': float, 'SES': str, 'HOME_PASSED': int,
#  'CUST_SINCE_DT': str, 'MONTHS_AGE': float, 'CANCEL_DT': str, 'CITY': str, 'POP': str,
#  'COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM': int, 'INBOUND_CALLS_NUM': int, 'KEYWORDS_NUM': int, 'VISITS_NUM': int,
#  'TECHSUPPORT_NUM': int, 'INTERACTIONS_NUM': int]

# Convert columns accordingly:
df_merged["CANCELED"] = df_merged["CANCELED"].astype(int)
df_merged["ROW_WID"] = df_merged["ROW_WID"].astype(int)
df_merged["ACCNT_LOC"] = df_merged["ACCNT_LOC"].astype(int)

df_merged["SES"] = df_merged["SES"].astype(str)

df_merged["MONTHS_AGE"] = df_merged["MONTHS_AGE"].astype(float)

# CANCEL_DT, CITY, POP are strings but may contain NaN - convert NaN to empty string or keep as is

df_merged["CITY"] = df_merged["CITY"].fillna("").astype(str)
df_merged["POP"] = df_merged["POP"].fillna("").astype(str)

# Step 6: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_8.csv", index_col=0)
source9 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/training_9.csv", index_col=0)

# UNION all source tables with the same schema (the big dimension tables)
dim_tables = [source0, source2, source6, source7]
dim_union = pd.concat(dim_tables, ignore_index=True)

# JOIN the unioned dimension table with all aspect tables on ROW_WID
# First, join with source1 (KEYWORDS_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(dim_union, source1, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Join with source3 (VISITS_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(joined, source3, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Join with source4 (COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(joined, source4, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Join with source5 (TECHSUPPORT_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(joined, source5, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Join with source8 (INBOUND_CALLS_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(joined, source8, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Join with source9 (INTERACTIONS_NUM)
joined = pd.merge(joined, source9, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Group by leftmost non-float columns that are unique identifiers in target examples:
# According to target schema and hints, group by:
# CANCELED (int), ROW_WID (int), ACCNT_LOC (int), SES (str), HOME_PASSED (int), CUST_SINCE_DT (str), CANCEL_DT (str), CITY (str), POP (str)
group_by_cols = [
    "CANCELED", "ROW_WID", "ACCNT_LOC", "SES", "HOME_PASSED",
    "CUST_SINCE_DT", "CANCEL_DT", "CITY", "POP"
]

# Aggregations:
# ARPU and MONTHS_AGE are floats, sum aggregation (per hint 13)
# COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM, INBOUND_CALLS_NUM, KEYWORDS_NUM, VISITS_NUM, TECHSUPPORT_NUM, INTERACTIONS_NUM are counts, sum aggregation
agg_dict = {
    "ARPU": "sum",
    "MONTHS_AGE": "sum",
    "COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM": "sum",
    "INBOUND_CALLS_NUM": "sum",
    "KEYWORDS_NUM": "sum",
    "VISITS_NUM": "sum",
    "TECHSUPPORT_NUM": "sum",
    "INTERACTIONS_NUM": "sum"
}

# Perform groupby and aggregation
result = joined.groupby(group_by_cols, dropna=False, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'CANCELED', 'ROW_WID', 'ACCNT_LOC', 'ARPU', 'SES', 'HOME_PASSED',
    'CUST_SINCE_DT', 'MONTHS_AGE', 'CANCEL_DT', 'CITY', 'POP',
    'COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM', 'INBOUND_CALLS_NUM', 'KEYWORDS_NUM',
    'VISITS_NUM', 'TECHSUPPORT_NUM', 'INTERACTIONS_NUM'
]

result = result[target_columns]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_24/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
